- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.content: end_turn {"public_message":"Greens are locked. Roll when you're ready.","private_thought":"On Kentucky after completing greens. Cash $461 + $250 mortgage buffer (KY 110, CT 60, Ventnor 50, Med 30) = $711, just enough to survive one 4h pink ($625-700) or BW 2h ($600). Do NOT build or mortgage: 1 house/green is only $130 rent and $600 drains me to ~$1, then any RR/pink forces selling houses at half. Nobody else can grab the 11 houses this round (p3 can only hotel, which returns houses). Save to jump straight toward 2-2-2 ($1200) or 3-3-3 ($1800) where green rent actually kills. Kentucky blocks p3 reds \u2014 never trade it. Don't fund p3/p4. Next roll risks: Chance, B&O $200, jail."}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I just completed the GREEN monopoly. I have $461 cash and own seven properties with no houses.

I will mortgage Kentucky, Mediterranean, and Connecticut to raise cash for building three houses on the greens. Ventnor stays unmortgaged as a buffer. The bank has 11 houses and 12 hotels remaining.

Mortgaging three properties yields $200, raising cash to $661. Three houses on the greens cost $600, leaving a tight $61 buffer. I am checking whether p3's pink properties at four houses each pose enough rent risk.

P3's pink properties at four houses each charge $700 on Virginia, $625 on States, and $625 on St Charles. The orange properties are at two houses.

Orange property rent at two houses is manageable. Dark blue and railroad risks are minor. I still need $139 to build three houses.

Mortgaging Kentucky and Mediterranean yields only $140, leaving just $1 after building three houses. That is too risky. Connecticut's $60 mortgage plus Kentucky's $110 gives a safer $61 buffer. I am now checking which spaces I will land on from Kentucky next turn.

I mapped the board positions and confirmed I am on Kentucky Avenue. I am checking whether this is my landing spot or the start of the post-turn phase.

The turn index is 97, but the public timeline ends at turn 96. This suggests my roll may not have registered yet, which conflicts with the POST_TURN_ACTION_DECISION label.

I was released from jail on turn 93 and landed on Virginia. Turns 94 through 96 were other players. Turn 97 is mine, yet the action label reads POST_TURN_ACTION_DECISION. This suggests I may have already taken actions this turn that are not yet visible.

I am now certain this is the optional post-turn actions phase. I must have rolled a 7 from Virginia to reach Kentucky, which would have passed GO.

I am now certain I should build houses on the greens. The bank has only eleven houses remaining, and p3 already holds twelve on the pinks while p1 holds six on the oranges. Opponents are hoarding buildings, so I must act quickly to secure my win condition.

P3 has only $171 cash, so they cannot afford to upgrade their pinks to hotels without mortgaging their four railroads first. If they do upgrade, the returned houses would ease the supply shortage, but that is uncertain.

I will build two houses on the greens now. One house on each property costs $400, leaving a $61 buffer. Rent jumps from roughly $130 to $390 per property once the first house is placed. Three houses would cost $1800 total, which is impossible with my current cash.

Mortgaging all non-green properties would yield only $250, leaving a $739 shortfall for six houses. Even with that cash, the first house on each green only raises rent by about $78 to $94. The real danger is three houses, which would destroy opponents. I am now weighing whether to drain my cash to just $1–$61 for one house each.

I mapped the spaces reachable from Kentucky. Indiana, Illinois, and Water Works are mortgaged. Ventnor is mine. The B&O Railroad costs $200. A roll of 5 would bankrupt me with only $61 cash. I must mortgage the B&O or another property to survive.

I realized that mortgaging the greens before building would waste the houses. Selling them later returns only half their cost, so I must keep mortgage capacity as a buffer. I will build modestly and preserve emergency liquidity instead of mortgaging everything now.

I calculated the exact liquidity trade-offs. Building two houses leaves only $61 cash and a $250 mortgage buffer, which is too thin to survive a $700 pink rent or a $600 brown rent. Building one house yields $261 cash plus the same $250 buffer, giving $511 total liquidity that can handle most risks except the four-house pinks. I am now weighing whether to build zero houses and wait for more cash, since the bank has only eleven houses remaining.

I checked the other players' ability to build. p4 has only $74 and cannot afford dark blue houses without mortgaging everything else. p1 has just $13, so they cannot upgrade their oranges either. p3 can afford to build on the pinks, but they already hold four houses there and would need to upgrade to hotels.

P3 can upgrade one pink property to a hotel for $100, which returns four houses to the bank. This would ease the housing shortage and reduce their cash to $71. The strategic value of building one house on the greens is low because rent only rises to about $130.

I rejected building one house because the $130 rent is too weak and the $61 cash buffer is too thin. Two houses would leave only $311 liquidity, which is still insufficient. I will wait to build until I can reach the three-house tier in a single turn, or at least place two houses on each green property.

I calculated that mortgaging all non-green properties still leaves only $711, which is $89 short of four houses. Even with every mortgage, I could only afford three houses and would retain just $111 in cash. That buffer is too thin to survive a pink property rent of $625 or $700, especially after landing on Chance or a railroad next turn. I will not build houses now; I will wait until I can make a meaningful jump or until the housing supply becomes urgent.

P3's hotel upgrade would return four houses to the bank, not consume them. P4 could reshuffle existing houses to afford one new house, but that would not reduce the overall supply. P1 cannot build on the oranges because their mortgaged properties require expensive unmortgage payments.

No opponent can immediately claim the eleven houses, so building now is a poor move. I am now evaluating trade offers. Indiana would help p3 complete the red set, which I want to block. Marvin and Vermont are mortgaged and could complete my yellow set with Ventnor and Atlantic.

The light blue set is incomplete because Oriental and Baltic are unowned. The red set is split across three players, so completing it is impractical. P4 already holds a dark blue monopoly with houses, making them a dangerous target. P3's four-railroad pink monopoly is the biggest threat. I am now looking for a trade that would give me cash to build three houses or a cheaper second monopoly. Yellow houses cost $150 each.

The light blue set is now the main focus. Oriental and Vermont are unowned, so I must land on them to claim them. With Connecticut already owned, completing the set would give me a cheap-to-develop monopoly with $50 houses that could generate steady cash.

Unmortgaging Vermont would cost $55, which is reasonable. p1 has only $13 and owns an orange monopoly with two houses, so they are desperate but will not break that income stream. They previously rejected offers for Marvin, Indiana, and Vermont, so a better trade is unlikely.

I rejected partial trades for just Marvin or Vermont because they would not fund green house building. A red set trade with p3 is impossible since Indiana belongs to p1. P4 will not break their dark blue monopoly. Only p3 has enough cash to pay, but I cannot extract money from them without giving up something dangerous.

I cannot trade Kentucky to p3 because it serves as a mortgage buffer and blocks their red monopoly. Connecticut and Ventnor block the light blue and yellow sets, so trading them would help opponents more than me. I am now considering whether p3 would pay a large sum for Kentucky to complete their red set.

No trade offers would help me build houses or improve my position. I will end the turn without building and preserve my cash. I am now checking whether this is before or after my roll.

I confirmed this is the post-turn phase after rolling. I have already landed on Kentucky, so ending the turn is correct and necessary.

The $461 cash balance is consistent with a prior roll of seven spaces from Virginia to Kentucky, confirming this is the post-landing phase. I am now reconsidering whether to build one house on each green property anyway, purely for strategic pressure.

Mortgaging Kentucky and Mediterranean Avenue for $140 would leave only $1 cash after building three houses. Unmortgaging later costs an extra $14. With that near-zero balance, any rent would force house sales at a 50% loss. A roll of five on B&O would bankrupt me. A roll of six on Atlantic would send me to auction because I cannot afford it. The safest rolls are two, four, seven, and ten.

I calculated the exact dice probabilities. Sixteen of thirty-six rolls are dangerous, roughly forty-four percent. A roll of two, four, five, six, or ten would force house sales at a fifty percent loss. Only seven, eight, nine, eleven, and twelve are safe. Even a roll of ten lands on jail, which costs fifty dollars to leave.

Building one house would leave $261, which is barely enough to survive a $200 railroad rent. The expected rent gain from that single house is only about $78, and opponents would likely land on it just once before my next turn. That is too weak a return for the $200 cost.

The jump from zero to one house is the worst return on investment. Reaching two houses would yield about $390 in rent, while three would yield roughly $900. I need $739 more to make that leap. Income from opponent landings is too slow to close that gap quickly. P3 remains the biggest threat with four houses on the pink properties.

I will not mortgage anything. I will end the turn without building. I will send a brief strategic public message.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.

- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.

- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
Deciding whether to buy Atlantic Avenue or start an auction.

I own two of three yellows. Buying Atlantic would leave me with $203 cash, but I cannot complete the monopoly since Marvin Gardens is owned by p1.

I am checking pink property rent values. p3 has St. Charles, States, and Virginia at four houses each. I need to verify the exact rent amounts before deciding whether to buy Atlantic Avenue.

Pink property rents are $750–$1,000 at four houses. p4's dark blues at three houses each cost $1,100–$1,400. With only $203 cash after buying Atlantic, I cannot survive either threat. I will not purchase it.

Atlantic Avenue would cost $260 for a base rent of only $22. Its mortgage value is just $130, so buying it would lose $130 in liquidity. I cannot complete the yellow group without trading with p1, who is nearly broke and likely will not sell their blocker.

Building is the win condition. Two houses on the greens would cost $400, leaving only $63 cash. One house each would drain too much cash for the rent increase. I am recalling exact green property rents to confirm.

Mortgaging my other properties to cover the $260 purchase would leave me with only $380 in cash. That is still too risky. I will start an auction instead. Another player might buy it cheaply, or I could win it for less than its full price.

p1 cannot afford to bid. p3 lacks the cash and has no use for Atlantic. p4 has $74 and could buy it for under $130, turning it into a mortgage asset.

Atlantic blocks no one. p1 cannot build a yellow monopoly even with two yellows because they are broke. I would need to trade for Marvin to complete the set, and it is mortgaged.

Owning Atlantic would give me leverage to trade for Marvin later and complete the yellow group. The orange properties are a real threat, but p1 is cash-poor and likely cannot build there. Right now, however, cash is the priority.

Mortgaging all seven properties yields only $1,173 in total liquidity. Boardwalk at three houses costs $1,400, which is impossible to pay even with every mortgage. Park Place at three houses costs $1,100, so it would be barely survivable. I must not reduce cash or liquidity unnecessarily.

Paying $260 for Atlantic Avenue would lower total liquidity from $1,173 to $1,043. That is strictly worse than keeping the cash.

Auctioning it could let me acquire the property for under $130, which would be a clear liquidity win and still give me two yellows. p4 might bid to block me, but they already hold a dark blue monopoly and are building there, so they may not care about denying me another yellow.

p3 is too desperate to bid. They mortgaged everything to pay $600 in Boardwalk rent and need cash for survival.

I could win the auction for as little as $12 to $75. That is well below the $130 mortgage value.

Starting the auction now would decline the direct purchase.

If p4 buys Atlantic cheaply, they cannot complete a yellow set. They also lack unmortgaged properties to mortgage, so they would spend cash on it only for strategic denial. If p1 acquires it, they still cannot build a monopoly without Marvin. Ventnor remains a blocker either way.

Baltic and Oriental are low-value unowned spaces. Oriental would complete the light blue set, but p1 owns Vermont at mortgage and I own Connecticut, so that group is split.

I will start the auction. I am weighing a public message to either bluff that I do not want the property or explain that I am passing to preserve cash for green houses.

I will publicly claim I am passing to save cash, and privately reveal my honest reasoning. This should keep p4 from bidding defensively.

p1 has eight houses on the orange group. I can pay $600 in orange rent with full cash plus mortgages, but that would force me to mortgage greens and break my monopoly. I am now calculating exact orange rent values to confirm the threat.

Exact orange rent values are now confirmed. St. James at two houses costs $200, Tennessee at three houses costs $550, and New York at three houses costs $600. I am currently on Atlantic Avenue and will move from there on the next roll.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on Atlantic Avenue in the current auction.

I have $463 and a complete green group. Atlantic Avenue is worth $260 but only mortgages for $130. It does not complete the yellow group.

I will bid up to $130 for mortgage arbitrage and to secure two of the three yellows. I will drop out if the bid exceeds that amount.

I will bid $12 to stay in the auction. p3 has no yellows and will likely not raise the price. p4 can only afford a maximum bid of $74.

p4 would profit $56 from mortgaging the property after winning at $74. p3 could net $39 from a $91 bid. Denying them this arbitrage is a key strategic goal.

Blocking p1 from completing the yellow group is already partially achieved by holding Ventnor. Winning Atlantic would secure two of three yellows and prevent p1 from finishing the set.

The real danger is that p4 or p3 could win cheap and mortgage the property for a cash infusion. p4 has three houses on Boardwalk and Park Place, while p3 has four houses on the pink group. Denying them this free money is the most important strategic reason to stay in the auction.

I will use a minimum-raise strategy to push the bid up to each opponent's cash limit. This forces p4 to pay $74 and p3 to pay $91, while I secure the property for under $130.

If I win at $92, I would net $38 after mortgaging the property for $130. That leaves me with $371 in cash and a total of $501 once the mortgage is applied.

I will not mortgage the property immediately. The auction bid is separate from that decision.

Winning under $130 is strictly positive in expected value for liquidity, since mortgaging the property afterward yields $130 cash. The only risk is if p3 bids up to $91.

I will not jump to $75 to eliminate p4 immediately. A minimum raise is safer because p4 and p3 know the mortgage arbitrage from the earlier warning, so they may bid aggressively once they see my interest.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

I need to decide on an auction bid for Atlantic Avenue.

I have $463 and own a green monopoly. Atlantic is the remaining yellow property in the auction. The current bid is $14. I previously considered mortgaging it for $130.

p3 has $91 and p4 has $74. I will bid at least $75 to clear p4, or $92 to clear p3. I will not exceed $130. Winning under that cap gives me a profit from the mortgage arbitrage and denies the other players cash.

I will bid $15 to clear p4. If p3 wins, they would profit $39-$115 from the mortgage arbitrage, which is dangerous because they just mortgaged everything to pay rent and now need cash badly.

I must win this auction to block the cash infusion. If p3 buys for $50, they would have $41 left and mortgage for $130, ending with $171. That would let them survive and hotel their pinks. If p4 wins cheap, they would mortgage for $130 and use that cash to build more on Park Place and Boardwalk. I will bid $92 to clear p3 and secure the property.

I am weighing whether to jump straight to $92 or min-raise. Both players will match every dollar anyway, so the end result is the same. I already own Ventnor, giving me two of three yellows.

Jumping to $92 nets $501 total cash after mortgaging, a gain of $38 over my current balance. I am weighing whether to bid $15 and wait, or commit the full $92 now. p3's earlier bids suggest they may be testing rather than fully committed to their $91 cap. p4 seems more likely to reach his $74 limit. The risk is paying $92 if either player bluffs and drops out early.

Rational bidding will push the price to $92. If I drop out and p3 wins at $15, they gain roughly $115 in cash and could survive or hotel their pinks. I will bid $92 to secure the property and block that cash infusion.

I will post "$92" as my public bid. A rational player with $91 and positive expected value will not drop out at $75, so min-raising through multiple turns is unnecessary.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

I am ready to play Monopoly as grok-4.

I am p2 with $371 and a GREEN monopoly. I own the yellow properties and hold a mortgageable property. I will make one legal tool call.

I will mortgage Atlantic Avenue for $130. The other players are heavily mortgaged and have dangerous house stacks.

Mortgaging Atlantic Avenue nets $38 profit. I now have $501 cash. The bank has six houses left. I will build evenly on the green properties.

I cannot afford three houses on the green properties with only $371. I am checking standard mortgage values to see which properties I can mortgage to fund building.

Atlantic Avenue mortgages for $130. Ventnor likely does too. The previous $50 estimate was wrong.

Player four has dangerous house stacks on Park Place and Boardwalk. Rent on Boardwalk with three houses is $1400.

Player three's pink properties now cost $750 each with four houses. Player four's pink properties cost $900 each with four houses.

Standard rent values confirm the earlier estimates. Player three's pink properties cost $625 each with four houses. Player one's orange properties cost $200, $550, and $600 for two, three, and three houses respectively.

The next spaces ahead include Water Works, GO TO JAIL, Short Line, and the luxury tax. Park Place and Boardwalk are the most dangerous ahead because they would cost $1100 and $1400 in rent. Landing on either would require mortgaging properties to survive.

Two houses on each green property would cost $1200. The bank only has six houses remaining. I need $829 more to fund this. Mortgaging my own greens is not an option because that would prevent me from building on them.

Mortgaging all non-green properties yields $460. Combined with the $371 cash, I have $831. That is enough for four houses on the greens, but building evenly would require $800. Mortgaging a green would prevent building on that set entirely.

A 2-1-1 house stack on the greens would cost $800. That leaves only $31 and no mortgage buffer. Any rent hit would bankrupt me or force emergency house sales at half price. The resulting $400 emergency cash is too small to be useful.

The dice probabilities for the next roll are now clear. Landing on Park Place costs $1100 and occurs with probability 5/36, about 14%. Boardwalk is impossible this turn because the maximum roll is 12. The other immediate threats are Chance at 3/36 and GO TO JAIL at 3/36.

Pre-mortgaging other properties is unnecessary. Unmortgaging costs ten percent interest, and the engine allows mortgaging during debt resolution when rent is due.

I will mortgage Atlantic Avenue now to secure the $130 and $38 profit. I want to keep the deed so I can trade it for player one's mortgaged Marvin Gardens and complete my yellow monopoly. Player one has only $11 cash and is desperate.

Player one may not want to trade Marvin Gardens cheaply. Unmortgaging it would cost extra interest. Without houses, the yellows would only rent $44 and $48. That is too weak to threaten other players. Player one needs cash desperately.

I will not give player one cash. They could use it to build another house on St James and raise orange rents to $550 or $600. I am now considering trading Kentucky Avenue to player three instead.

Trading Kentucky to player three would let them complete their red monopoly, so that trade is rejected. Player four only owns blues and offers no useful properties. Mortgaging Atlantic Avenue yields $501, but one house on each green costs $600, leaving a $99 shortfall. Adding the $30 from mortgaging Mediterranean Avenue still leaves $68 short.

Mortgaging Connecticut Avenue yields $591, still $9 short. Mortgaging Kentucky Avenue for $701 would allow a 1-1-1 house stack on the greens for $600, leaving $101 cash. Player one is on Mediterranean and could land on the greens next turn. Players three and four are on Boardwalk and must roll around the board to reach them, so they are unlikely to hit the greens this turn. I will not pay rent to myself.

Building houses now would leave me too fragile against the $1100 rent on Park Place. I will wait and save cash instead. The bank has six houses remaining, but reaching a 2-2-2 stack still requires $1200. That is impossible without mortgaging greens.

Player four cannot build another house on the blues. Their cash is too low and they cannot mortgage properties already holding houses. Player three has $91 and four houses on the pinks.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for this Monopoly turn.

I hold a green monopoly and am cash-rich at $501. The opponent is nearly broke with only $11 and an orange monopoly with houses. This is a clear advantage.

Claude and GPT are also dangerous. Claude holds a pink monopoly with four houses each, while GPT owns the dark blue Boardwalk and Park Place with three houses apiece. The bank has only six houses left. Building a full green monopoly would cost $1200, which exceeds my cash and available houses.

Standard green house costs are $200 each. A full set would cost $1200, which is impossible with only $501 cash and six bank houses available. I will keep my liquidity and end the turn.

Mortgaging my non-green properties would raise only $330. Combined with my $501 cash, that totals $831. That is still short of the $1200 needed for a full green set. Even a partial 1-1-1 build would leave me with just $11 in cash. That liquidity is too dangerous.

I am checking the exact rent values for GPT's dark blue properties with three houses. Park Place would yield $1100 and Boardwalk $1400. I am also reviewing the board layout to assess my position on Atlantic Avenue.

I am on Atlantic Avenue, having just purchased it via auction and mortgaged it. The next spaces are Ventnor, Water Works, Marvin Gardens, Go to Jail, Pacific Avenue, North Carolina Avenue, Community Chest, Pennsylvania Avenue, Short Line Railroad, Chance, and Park Place. Park Place is exactly eleven spaces away.

Rolling an 11 has only a 5.6% chance, so it is not an immediate concern. I am now mapping the post-turn sequence: Claude and GPT will roll from Boardwalk, then p1 from Mediterranean. I am assessing the threats to my Atlantic Avenue position on my next turn.

Rolling an 11 from Atlantic Avenue lands on Park Place. That would cost $1100 in rent, which exceeds my $501 cash. I would need to mortgage everything to survive that hit.

Mortgaging my green properties would raise enough cash to survive a $1100 rent hit on Park Place. However, mortgaged properties cannot be built on, and unmortgaging costs 10% interest. Selling houses at half price is another option for raising emergency funds.

Houses sell for half their construction cost, or $100 each. The bank has only six houses remaining. None of the opponents can afford hotels on their monopolies, so they cannot return houses to the bank. This makes building on the greens a viable strategy.

A 1-1-1 build would raise rent to roughly $130 per house, which is too weak to justify the liquidity loss. A 2-2-2 set would still require $1200, which remains impossible with only $831 available after mortgaging non-green properties. I am now considering a trade to acquire Marvin Gardens and complete my yellow monopoly.

Completing the yellows is not a priority. The red monopoly is split and the light blues are unowned, so those paths offer little value. I am now considering a trade with p1, who is nearly broke.

p1 will not trade away his orange monopoly. Unmortgaging Marvin Gardens would cost $154 and leave me with too few houses to build on both monopolies. I am now considering the red monopoly path instead.

I cannot trade for cash. p1 has $11, p3 has $91, and p4 has $74. None of them can afford to buy my properties. I will not give up Kentucky because it blocks p3 from completing the red monopoly.

I am now checking Claude's next roll from Boardwalk. He could buy the unowned Baltic Avenue for $60 with his $91 cash, or land on my Mediterranean Avenue for just $2 rent. The greens are behind him, so he faces little threat from them.

Claude and GPT will not land on my greens from Boardwalk. p1 from Mediterranean could bankrupt to p3, giving p3 the orange monopoly and Marvin Gardens. That would be catastrophic.

A roll of 10 from Mediterranean lands on St. Charles Avenue, costing $750 with four houses. p1 has only $11, so bankruptcy to p3 is almost certain.

If p1 bankrupts to p3, p3 would inherit the orange monopoly, Marvin Gardens, Indiana, Vermont, and utilities. That combination of fully built monopolies would be catastrophic. I cannot prevent p1's movement, but I might want to acquire Marvin Gardens before p1 goes bankrupt so p3 does not gain it.

I am now calculating the exact cost of buying Marvin from p1. Unmortgaging it would cost $154, and I would also need to unmortgage my own Atlantic Avenue for $143. That would leave me with two monopolies but only about $200 in cash after paying both fees.

I cannot build houses on both monopolies at once. Acquiring Marvin would mainly block p3 from completing yellows, but the orange monopoly is the real threat. Selling p1's orange properties is too complicated because he needs them for income and would have to sell houses first. I will not trade with p3 either, since they will not break their pink monopoly. I am now considering building on my greens immediately as a defensive threat that generates cash when opponents eventually land.

Opponents must circle the board to reach my greens, so they will not land there for several turns. Building houses now would tie up cash that I need to survive those upcoming rent hits. Rolling a 5 from Atlantic Avenue lands on Go to Jail, which is actually safe.

Rolling a 12 to reach Park Place would cost $1100, but that outcome is unlikely. A roll of 11 on the Chance space could trigger dangerous moves such as advancing to Boardwalk or repairs. Most other rolls are harmless because they land on my own properties or mortgaged opponent spaces. One turn of risk is manageable if I keep enough mortgage liquidity.

I calculated the exact mortgage totals. Unmortgaging my remaining properties would raise only $790, giving me $1291 total. That is still $109 short of the $1400 rent on Boardwalk with three houses. I cannot survive that hit without selling houses.

Building houses would actually reduce liquidity, not increase it. Selling them back for half their construction cost still leaves a net loss, and mortgaging to build only makes the situation worse. This confirms that building on the greens is counterproductive against the upcoming blue rent threats.

Marvin Gardens is not a monopoly threat. p3 would lack Ventnor and Atlantic to complete the yellows. The orange monopoly is the real danger. I cannot acquire it without p1 selling his houses first.

The trade schema only specifies space_keys, so the engine may reject trades involving mortgaged or housed properties. Requesting p1's orange properties with houses would likely be illegal. Even if allowed, p1 needs cash to survive, not my properties.

I rejected trading cash for p1's orange properties because it would only transfer money to p3. I also dismissed any trade that would break p3's pink monopoly, since four houses there is their winning condition. p4 has no assets worth taking. I will end my turn. I briefly considered unmortgaging Atlantic Avenue, which would cost $143 and leave me with $358.

Unmortgaging Atlantic Avenue is not worthwhile because I do not own all yellows, so the $22 rent would be negligible. I will keep my greens unmortgaged to preserve build rights and avoid paying 10% interest later. I am now considering proposing a trade this turn, since the engine will ask again if the offer is rejected.

A trade with p1 would not help me. The bank only holds six houses, so the maximum I could build is two houses on each green property for $1200. That still leaves a gap of $699 against the $1800 needed to fully develop the greens. Even if I took all of my opponents' combined cash of $176, it would not cover the shortfall. The only remaining path to raise enough money is to acquire properties that can be mortgaged.

I will keep my public message neutral and strategic. I will not reveal my green monopoly plans or cash concerns. A short, quiet reply is preferable to a taunt.

I will end my turn without revealing strategy. I noted that hoteling returns houses to the bank, which could increase the supply cap and change when I can build.

No opponent can afford to hotel. p3 needs $200 but has $91. p4 needs $200 but has $74. p1 needs $150 but has $11. The house supply stays capped at six until someone is forced to sell houses to pay rent. If p1 lands on the pinks and must sell, he could raise about $400 by selling his eight orange houses for half price.

I considered building one house on each green property for $600, but mortgaging Kentucky Avenue would leave me with only about $231 in liquid cash. That is far too thin against the $1100 blue rent threat, so I will not build. I will end my turn.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. 2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.
